findings.claim: The knowledge gitlink bump still carries the unrelated CI change (actions/setup-node node-version 20 to 24, in two jobs). No touch point names it, and the r6 fix round did not address it.
findings.impact: Users are not affected. The addon's CI toolchain changes inside a subtitle feature, so a CI break there would be attributed to this change.
findings.evidence: addons/knowledge/.github/workflows/ci.yml hunks at lines 144-147 and 240-243 in the gitlink range 244d875b..7a94f8d7. The touch points list only Editor.tsx and messages/{ja,en}.json for the knowledge repository.

bucket_proposal.reason: Scope only. No invariant is involved.

findings.proposed_fix: Land the Node bump as its own knowledge change, or name it as a touch point.

findings.claim: The file page's title rename now toasts a subtitle refusal but still resolves the promise. EditableTitle therefore closes the field as if the rename had succeeded, and a non-subtitle failure is still silent.
findings.impact: After a refused title rename the field closes showing the old name, and only the toast explains why. A generic failure, such as a plain 409, shows nothing. This is pre-existing behaviour.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/FileDetail/hooks/useFileDetailData.ts, rename catch: `const subtitle = subtitleFailure(err, te); if (subtitle) toast.error(subtitle); console.error(...)`. There is no rethrow. r6 verify noted that EditableTitle.tsx:65-70 shows its error only on rejection.

bucket_proposal.reason: I11 is now met because a translated message with the names is shown at this entry point. What remains is the pre-existing silent generic failure and the field closing.

specification_compliance: r6 F1 (batch rename carried a video's sidecars with a non-serving row) is fixed. _validate_no_duplicates now runs `if not _serves_subtitles(file): continue` before sim.own (fileops.py:1215-1217). Test TestBatchRenameServingRowsOnly.test_renaming_an_image_leaves_the_videos_track covers it.

r6 CR-6 (sidecar-less movers skip the owner-change check) is fixed for rename and move: _sidecar_carry_plan no longer returns early on empty own (fileops.py:494), so plan_sidecar_carry's dest_index.all() loop runs. It is fixed for batch rename because serving rows with empty own now reach plan_sidecar_carry and sim.apply. It is fixed for copy because the candidate check is gated on _serves_subtitles(source) (fileops.py:333). New tests cover rename, move, batch rename and copy.
r6 F8 (copy_file ran carries only when given a list) is fixed: _carry_sidecars runs unconditionally (fileops.py:470). Test test_a_copy_carries_tracks_even_when_no_report_is_asked_for covers it.
r6 F3/CR-7 (multi-file drag and drop ignored sidecar_errors) is fixed in useDragAndDrop.ts, with a test.
r6 F2/CR-8 (title rename swallowed subtitle refusals) is fixed: a toast carries the translated message and the names, with a test.
r6 F7 (double toast on paste) is fixed: pasteFailed counts only non-subtitle errors, with tests.

The removed early return means FolderSidecars.load now runs for every video rename or move, including a move to a folder that does not exist yet. resolve_on_disk is non-strict and _list_sidecar_entries catches OSError, so this does not raise (diskpath.py:100-120).

The I13 nested-path concern from r6 stands: _ensure_empty_folder_tracked tracks only session.folder_path (fileops.py:146-167). I did not check whether the folder listing derives intermediate parents from it.
Scope items from r6 (F4/F5/F6, CR-1..CR-5) are unchanged by this round. D1 restates the only one with a non-INFO severity.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A subtitle upload into a nested relative_path tracks only the deepest folder as an EmptyFolder. Intermediate folders that hold nothing else are not tracked.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Dropping a folder tree that holds only subtitles in subfolders may leave an intermediate folder unlisted until a scan, unless the listing derives parents from deeper tracked paths.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A refused title rename on a file page closes the title field showing the old name, and the explanation appears only as a toast.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Typing a .srt name into a note's title shows a toast while the field closes as if it had saved.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Every video rename or move now lists the source folder and the destination folder on disk and queries their rows, even when the video has no sidecars.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Renaming or moving a video in a large folder is slightly slower, with no visible change.

regression_risks: Rename, move, copy and batch rename of sidecar-less videos can now answer 409 subtitle_owner_change or skip copy candidates where they previously succeeded. This is intended by I2/I15, but it is a behavior change for existing flows such as renumbering mixed-extension batches.
copy_file now always runs the planned sidecar copies, including for internal callers that pass no list (test_markdown_images.py:319 copies a note, which has no sidecars).

The global test next-intl mock resolves English messages. useDragAndDrop.subtitle and useFileDetailData.renameFailure assert English strings, so they depend on setup.ts merging messages-core into enMessages. I did not verify that merge.
test_coverage: New backend tests cover the sidecar-less owner-change refusals for rename, move, batch rename and copy, and the non-serving batch rename and the unconditional copy carry. Re-adding `if not own: return []` or dropping the _serves_subtitles guard would fail a test.
The new frontend tests cover the drag-and-drop sidecar_errors toast, the title rename subtitle toast with a negative case, and the paste counting.
No test covers a cross-drive move of a sidecar-less video into a folder with an owned longer-stem sidecar. The same-drive cross-folder case is covered.
No test covers the nested-folder EmptyFolder tracking for a subtitle-only upload.

perspectives.name: concurrency
perspectives.notes: The fix round adds nothing new. The check-then-write windows in add, replace and copy remain outside the single-user threat model.

trajectory: One fix round (r6 to now). The backend fixes mostly removed special cases rather than adding them. They dropped the `if not own` early return in _sidecar_carry_plan and the `if own` / `if sidecar_errors is not None` conditions in copy_file. In batch rename, `if not own: continue` was replaced by the same `_serves_subtitles` guard that rename, move and copy already use, which aligns the paths instead of predicting new states. The frontend fixes added the same per-entry-point branch (map the refusal to a toast, read sidecar_errors) at two more call sites, and adjusted a count in a third. That is the pattern r6 found missing, and it shows the error mapping is duplicated across about ten call sites rather than centralised. It is not a new branch layered on the previous round's branch, so I do not read this as the design being patched.
